title: THE DANGER OF GREED AND A CONSCIENCE CONDEMNED

memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: "Then Judas, his betrayer, seeing that He had been condemned, was remorseful and brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders..." —Matthew 27:3

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text: The tragedy of Judas Iscariot serves as a sobering reminder of how destructive unbridled greed can be. Even though he was an active partaker in ministry, worked miracles alongside the other disciples, and walked as a close friend to Jesus Himself, his weakness for money ultimately overtook everything. When Judas realized the magnitude of his sin, he confessed his wrong to the chief priests, seeking a measure of relief from his heavy heart. Yet, the world offers no true mercy to those it uses; the chief priests coldly dismissed him, stating it was up to him and leaving him completely alone in his agonizing despair. Overwhelmed by remorse and a conscience condemned beyond what he could bear, Judas took his own life, sealing his tragic destiny through his own decisions influenced by Satan. This harrowing account illustrates that material obsession can blind a person to divine grace and spiritual truth. Greed does not merely steal contentment; it makes a person wander, leads to slander, and can ultimately drive one toward destructive, murderous actions. True spiritual safety requires us to guard our hearts jealously against the love of wealth and possessions. We must choose instead to find our total satisfaction in the presence and provision of God. Being content with what we have allows us to live a life of joy, peace, and continuous praise to our Creator.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: "So be careful on greed on money it make you to wander slander and even leads to murderous actions. Be content what you have and be merry and give praise to God for what you have."

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Heavenly Father, protect our hearts from the deceitfulness of wealth and the trap of greed. Help us to be deeply content with what You have provided, filling our days with praise and keeping us anchored firmly in Your grace. In Jesus' name, Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Guard your heart against earthly distractions today, and let gratitude and contentment fill every corner of your life.
